itinerary.summary: A sunrise boat, the old city, and the evening aarti.

place.name: Sunrise boat along the ghats
place.description: Row from Assi Ghat downstream at dawn as bathers, priests and washermen start the day, past Manikarnika, the burning ghat that never goes out.

morning.tip: Agree the boat price and route at Assi the night before; photography at the cremation ghats is not allowed.

place.name: Kashi Vishwanath and the old lanes
place.description: Walk the rebuilt corridor to the golden-spired Shiva temple, then lose yourself in the galis for kachori-sabzi and lassi at Blue Lassi.

afternoon.tip: Phones, bags and pens aren't allowed inside the temple; use the lockers near the gate.

place.name: Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat
place.description: Seven priests perform the fire ritual in unison with lamps, conch shells and chants. Watch from the steps or from a boat on the river.

evening.tip: A boat view (₹100-200 each) avoids the crush on the steps.

itinerary.dayTip: Wear slip-on shoes; you'll take them off often.

itinerary.summary: The Buddha's first sermon site, silk workshops, and a last walk on the ghats.

place.name: Sarnath
place.description: Ten kilometres north, the deer park where the Buddha gave his first teaching, with the great Dhamek Stupa and a museum holding the Lion Capital, India's national emblem.

morning.tip: The museum is closed on Fridays.

place.name: Banarasi silk weavers
place.description: Visit a family handloom workshop to see Banarasi brocade being woven thread by thread, and buy direct from the weavers.

afternoon.tip: Ask to see the GI tag for genuine Banarasi silk.

place.name: Assi Ghat evening
place.description: A gentler aarti and evening music at Assi Ghat, then dinner at a rooftop café overlooking the river.

evening.tip: Try malaiyo, saffron milk foam, if you're here Nov-Feb; it's only made in winter.

stays.name: BrijRama Palace
stays.why: An 18th-century palace right on the ghats, reached by boat.

stays.name: Ganges View Hotel
stays.why: A long-loved guesthouse with river-facing rooms and music evenings.

stays.name: Zostel Varanasi
stays.why: Budget beds close to the ghats.

essentials.currency: Indian Rupee (INR). UPI and cards work in towns; carry cash for small temples, coracles and rural stalls.
essentials.language: Hindi and Bhojpuri; English understood in tourist areas
essentials.tipping: Small tips for boatmen and guides
essentials.weather: Oct-Mar is best (8-28°C); winter mornings are foggy and atmospheric.
essentials.gettingAround: Walk the ghats; cycle-rickshaws and e-ricks for the city; a cab for Sarnath.
essentials.phrase: Har Har Mahadev: the city's greeting to Shiva

packing: Warm layer for dawn boats in winter

summary.overview: Two intense, beautiful days in one of the world's oldest living cities: a dawn boat along the ghats, the Kashi Vishwanath corridor, old-city food lanes, the Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh and a quiet morning at Sarnath.
highlights: Dawn boat ride along the ghats
The Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat
Kachori and malaiyo in the old lanes
Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught
